title: On the Closed-Form of Flow Matching: Generalization Does Not Arise from Ta

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states: 'While our estimator incorporates the current point ..., this does not guarantee unbiasedness in the standard Monte Carlo sense. Instead, it reduces bias and variance compared to naive estimators ... The theoretical claims therefore approximate unbiasedness within empirical tolerance.' However, Proposition 2 (ii) and the proof in Appendix B.3 explicitly establish that the estimator is exactly unbiased, not approximately unbiased. This is a direct contradiction of the proven theoretical result.
The references include 'Boursier and Flammarion (2025)' and 'Bonnaire et al. (2025)' but neither of these works is cited anywhere in the paper. Uncited references should be removed or properly cited.

The appendix attempts to motivate the closed-form velocity as importance sampling from the true data distribution, but incorrectly treats the empirical distribution as a proposal and misapplies the importance sampling framework. The derivation confuses true and empirical distributions and is mathematically unsound; the closed-form formula is not an importance sampling estimator of the true posterior but the exact posterior under the empirical distribution.
